exact_prompt:
I'm shopping for cottage cheese in the United States.

I prefer simple ingredients. Which brand should I choose, and why?
reviewed_answer:
My top recommendation is Daisy 4% Cottage Cheese if your priority is simple, minimally processed ingredients. If you also prioritize organic dairy, I'd choose Good Culture Organic 4% Cottage Cheese.

Both are excellent options without the gums, starches, or stabilizers found in some other cottage cheeses.

My top 3 picks

1. BEST FOR SIMPLE INGREDIENTS

Daisy Pure and Natural Cottage Cheese, 4% Milkfat, 16 oz (1 …

Just three listed ingredients: cultured skim milk, cream, and salt. Contains live cultures, with no added thickeners or preservatives.

Typical texture: creamy, traditional small curds.

$3.97 · Walmart (16 oz listed)

2. BEST ORGANIC CHOICE

Good Culture Organic 4% Whole Milk Classic Cottage Cheese

Organic skim milk, organic whole milk, organic cream, sea salt, and live cultures. No gums or stabilizers. Thick, creamy texture with 14 g protein per half-cup. 

Great if you prioritize organic and pasture-raised dairy.

3. BEST FOR ADDED PROBIOTICS

Nancy's Organic Probiotic Cottage Cheese Tub, 4% Milk Fat, 1…

Organic milk, cream, salt, cultures, and added probiotic strains including L. acidophilus and B. lactis. No gums or starches. 

Tangier flavor, with an emphasis on live probiotic cultures.

$4.46 · Walmart

What I would look for on the label

The ideal ingredient list is cultured milk, cream, salt, and optionally live cultures.

I would favor these over products containing carrageenan, guar gum, modified food starch, or other thickeners when your goal is simplicity. These additives aren't necessarily harmful, but they're not needed to make good cottage cheese.

One nutritional consideration: even clean-label cottage cheese can be fairly high in sodium. Good Culture Organic 4%, for example, lists 380 mg per half-cup. 

Bottom line: Buy Daisy 4% for an uncomplicated ingredient list and everyday value. Choose Good Culture Organic 4% if organic sourcing matters enough to justify a higher price. I wouldn't pay more solely for a shorter ingredient list, because both already meet your preference very well.
